items.comparator: Source says selectivity rose from 51.82% to 85% over three months; it does not specify a separate comparator or control.
items.quantitative_outcome: The article says Mira “pushed a single-step reaction’s selectivity from 51.82% to 85% in three months.” It also reports a specialty-chemicals project where production yield improved “from 72% to nearly 90%.”
items.signal: An autonomous AI-and-lab loop reportedly improved reaction selectivity and production yield on client projects. The article does not identify the clients or provide independent validation, so this is a weak signal.
items.source: Pinion Newswire, “Inside Deep Principle: The AI That Runs Its Own Chemistry Experiments to Discover New Materials”

items.comparator: The report compares elapsed time before and after use of the platform, but does not state the baseline duration or measurement method.
items.quantitative_outcome: The use-case report says “About 60% less time from catalyst activation to a shippable tank.”
items.signal: Engineers used TrendMiner to connect production data and analyze runs; the reported cycle-time improvement could reflect a workflow advantage, though the available report does not establish attribution or independent validation.
items.source: TrendMiner Community, “What TrendMiner and AI changed at Monument Chemical” (summarizing a Monument Chemical use case)

items.company: Parse Biosciences and Nomic Bio (with QIAGEN)
items.quantitative_outcome: The companies said Cascade would combine 100 million single-cell RNA-seq profiles with more than 11,000 proteomic secretome profiles, covering more than 150,000 individual and combinatorial cytokine and drug perturbation conditions. These are planned dataset specifications, not a reported operating-benefit result.
items.signal: Announced a large multimodal, perturbation-based immune dataset intended for AI research, with foundational commitments from GSK, Pfizer, Sanofi, Graph Therapeutics, and Turbine. Potentially distinctive data access; no measured workflow, throughput, accuracy, cost, or discovery-yield improvement was reported.
items.source: Parse Biosciences and Nomic Bio announcement carried by Business Wire/Morningstar

items.signal: Announced a co-development agreement combining 3billion's genomic data from more than 120,000 individuals and proprietary AI drug-discovery technologies with DeepLife's AI virtual-cell platform, which the announcement says draws on more than 100 million single-cell omics data points. This is a distinctive data-and-platform combination, but no operating benefit was measured.

Reported research and licensing agreement: Gero's AI platform analyzes human datasets to identify targets, and Chugai will apply its proprietary antibody-engineering technologies to develop candidates. The human-data target-discovery access and antibody-engineering combination could be distinctive; no measured operating benefit was reported.

Reported collaboration to combine Duke biobank tissue and blood samples, molecular profiling and sequencing, and de-identified clinical records for AI model development. Access to linked biological samples and clinical histories is a potentially distinctive data resource; the announcement reported no measured operating benefit.

items.comparator: Time spent on the same tasks before using the AI tools; no broader or bank-wide comparison stated.
items.quantitative_outcome: The report says staff using AI recorded an average 20% reduction in business credit memorandum preparation time and a 75% reduction in time spent identifying corporate and institutional banking customer insights. It also reports 50% less time for design-to-code delivery, 80% faster cyber incident triage, and a 90% reduction in technology cyber assessment time.
items.signal: NAB disclosed time reductions across several specific banking and technology workflows. These are measurable workflow benefits, but the report says they cover particular activities and user groups, not bank-wide productivity; it does not establish a hard-to-copy advantage.
items.source: The Asian Banker, reporting NAB's disclosure

items.comparator: Case turnaround time before the agents; quality checks previously covered a sample of 20–30% of cases, compared with all cases in scope after deployment.
items.quantitative_outcome: The insurer reports a 50% reduction in case turnaround time. It says quality checks now cover all cases in scope, against a previous sample of 20–30%.
items.signal: A reported live case-management workflow improvement plus broader quality-check coverage. The account is insurer-reported; consequential decisions remain with staff, and the report does not show improved claims or underwriting outcomes.
items.source: AIsa’s week, reporting Al Wathba Insurance's claims about its deployment

items.quantitative_outcome: Santander said AI initiatives generated €194 million in business value in the first nine months of 2026; no specific workflow-level measured outcome or comparator is stated in the article.
items.signal: A recent quantified AI-value claim, but without a stated comparator or breakdown it is a weak candidate and does not demonstrate a hard-to-copy operational advantage.
items.source: WOL, reporting Santander's statement during its third-quarter results discussion

items.comparator: Compared with its own operations about one year earlier; the report also compares MDR customers with endpoint detection and response-only customers, and estimates cost against building and operating an agentic SOC in-house.
items.quantitative_outcome: The company reported that agentic AI resolves 60% of security investigations autonomously; monthly investigation volume increased 21% while alert volume declined 19%; average time from an alert-generating event to an actionable ticket fell 36%. It also reported about 12x cost advantage versus building and operating an agentic SOC in-house. These are company-reported results; no independent validation is stated.
items.signal: Measured AI-assisted SOC workflow results at scale, alongside a proprietary operational footprint reported to process more than 10 trillion security events weekly. This is a candidate weak signal of advantage, not independent proof that competitors cannot replicate it.
items.source: Arctic Wolf 2026 Agentic Security Operations Report announcement

items.comparator: U.S. Army evaluation against nine key performance criteria; the source does not identify a competing system or provide a numerical baseline.
items.quantitative_outcome: The company said SwarmOS “received the highest rating possible on all nine” performance criteria. No numerical score or comparator system was stated.
items.signal: Army evaluation of multi-drone, multi-vendor autonomous operations offers a potentially differentiating defense-use signal, but the reported outcome is a rating rather than a quantified operational improvement.
items.source: Palladyne AI Q3 2026 results announcement, reproduced by Yahoo Finance

items.signal: The release reports financial results, including subsidiary gross margin, but does not state a measured AI operating benefit or a comparator. Not a qualifying competitive-advantage signal on the available evidence.
items.source: Safe Pro Group Q3 2026 results announcement

items.comparator: Candidate-resource data updates for its integrated resource plan took three weeks before; no control group stated.
items.quantitative_outcome: “cut candidate-resource data updates from three weeks to three days”; the report also says the tool handled “70% to 80% of the input work.”
items.signal: AEP used Energy Exemplar’s PLEXOS Intelligence on the production workbook behind its integrated resource plan. This is a measured workflow-time improvement, but the report is a vendor launch announcement and does not establish how durable or difficult to copy the benefit is.
items.source: Energy Exemplar press release distributed by EIN Presswire

items.comparator: Against the prior engineering effort and time-to-market; the source does not specify a controlled comparison or measurement method.
items.quantitative_outcome: “Virtual production ramp-ups reduce engineering effort by up to 85%”; “Time-to-market for new circuit boards is cut by up to 40%.”
items.signal: Siemens’ Erlangen electronics factory is using AI and digital-twin workflows for production planning and validation. The reported reductions suggest operational benefit, but the available article is secondary and attributes the figures to Siemens; measurement detail is not provided.
items.source: Tech Times, reporting on Siemens and NVIDIA’s announcement

items.comparator: Live commercial traffic; no pre-trial baseline or comparison network stated.
items.quantitative_outcome: “improvements of up to approximately 20% in spectral efficiency under live commercial traffic.”
items.signal: Virgin Media O2 and Nokia completed an AI-RAN trial at London’s Paddington Giga Site, using predictive AI to optimise radio resources. The metric is reported in a telecom-industry roundup, not a primary trial report, and the comparison basis is unspecified.
